name: Iru
hail: Both peoples of Iru greet you. Two voices, one world. Why not three?
The Sea Iru and the Hill Iru greet the Third, together. We speak for both, and only for both.
From the tidal flats and from the hills, both of us greet you, Third.
close: The Sea Iru and the Hill Iru, in Concord.
finding: Found by one people, checked by the other: {part}
We found, that is, both of us found: {part}
{part} Sea and Hill measured it, each in its own way.
Checked from the shore and from the heights: {part}
{part} Two kinds of mind, one answer.
sighting: {part} The shore saw it, and the hills saw it.
{part} We each looked. We each saw the same.
Sea Iru and Hill Iru, watching together: {part}
archive: From the Concord's records, kept by both: {part}
{part} The Sea Iru kept this, and the Hill Iru kept it too.
{part} Each people holds a copy. We send it together.
culture: About us, which is to say, about both of us: {part}
{part} We say we. We mean both.
Of the Sea Iru and the Hill Iru together: {part}
Since the Concord, this is true of both of us: {part}
{part} Two peoples, one world. It took practice.
request: {part} The Sea Iru and the Hill Iru will read your reply together.
{part} Both of us agreed to ask it. That is not nothing.
On behalf of Sea and Hill alike: {part}
verdict: {part} Sea and Hill are of one mind on this.
Weighed by the Sea Iru, weighed by the Hill Iru: {part}
{part} This is said for both, as the Concord requires.
accord: We know accords. Ours has held a long time. {part}
In the spirit of the Concord: {part}
Sea and Hill, together, on this accord: {part}
{part} Each of us holds a veto. Neither used it.
